newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak finmin 4-wk T-bill average yield 19.29 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovak finmin 4-wk T-bill average yield 19.29 pct.

text.p: The average yield at a Slovak finance ministry four-week treasury bill auction on Wednesday rose to 19.287 percent from 13.52 percent in the previous auction of four-week T-bills on June 25.
The ministry accepted bids worth 1.257 billion crowns out of total demand of 2.157 billion crowns, the central bank, said in a statement.
The minimum accepted rate was 17.60 percent while the maximum rate hit 20.00 percent.
In the last auction of T-bills with a similar maturity on July 23 a 725 million crown tranche of three-week notes was sold at an average yield of 18.196 percent.
The ministry on Wednesday also issued a 4.2 billion crown tranche of one-week treasury bills to the NBS portfolio.
The central bank often offers last resort help in covering the state budget deficit by buying finance ministry T-bills.

According to current legislation, the NBS can hold in its portfolio state paper worth up to five percent of budget revenues in the previous fiscal year. Budget revenues totalled 166.3 billion crowns in 1996.
The ministry does not set an amount on offer in state securities auctions, nor does it set a minimum or maximum limit price on bids.

It uses T-bills and state bonds as the main tools to cover the state budget deficit, which widened to 17.936 billion crowns for the first seven months of this year from 13.209 billion in the January-June period of 1997.
